speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the high-rise anti-littering measures taken so far have been effective; (b) whether the surveillance devices being deployed can be scaled up; and (c) whether the agencies will look to new technologies and devices to enhance enforcement capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA adopts a multi-pronged approach comprising enforcement, public education and community partnerships to deter high-rise litterbugs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA will continue to enhance its enforcement capabilities by keeping pace with developments in camera technology for high-rise littering surveillance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Even as NEA steps up enforcement against high-rise littering, we must continue to cultivate social graciousness, good habits and a sense of collective responsibility to keep Singapore clean and safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For this reason, NEA adopts complementary strategies such as strengthening community partnerships to raise awareness on the negative impacts of high-rise littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In 2020, NEA trialled informative standees at public areas with persistent littering feedback and enforcement, to deter people from committing high-rise littering offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA is also partnering Town Councils to install posters at HDB blocks, highlighting the environmental and social consequences of high-rise littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Through the collective efforts of all, we can uphold high standards of public cleanliness.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: While I appreciate the efforts by NEA over the years, there are obviously no visible improvements in the estate that we can see and have been monitoring.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Items continue to be thrown out of windows, such as cigarette butts, and it is frequently still happening.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Many Members have raised this in this House for many years.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether this is a case where the deterrent effect is not working and the litterbugs think they can get away with it.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: If that is the case, then are surveillance and enforcement working to achieve that?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Again, let me thank the Member for his questions and, in fact, comments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, with regard to the question about the deterrent effect of our enforcements, let me say that due to the nature of the offence – high-rise littering act – as well as the fact that our estates especially are very heavily built up, very dense, I think you would appreciate that it is not easy to identify and apprehend high-rise litterbugs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Despite this, a high-rise littering offence is a very serious offence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It affects our public health and, in fact, safety, too, and we take this seriously and we take firm enforcement action as far as is possible and practicable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over the years, we have stepped up our enforcement and surveillance capabilities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, we have worked to improve our work processes through data analytics so that we can actually shorten the waiting time for camera deployments for surveillance and that is the reason why we are able to increase the number of deployments of the cameras.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also worked to streamline our investigation procedures to shorten the investigation period as far as possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we are doing now is also to deter future high-rise litterbugs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said earlier, at the end of the day, even as we step up enforcement and continue to actively monitor and try and apprehend with technology and so on, ultimately, what is important is we need the community, we need Singaporeans to cooperate.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need Singaporeans to cultivate social graciousness, good habits and collective responsibility and not to litter, in order to be able to keep Singapore clean and green.
